operators()

The operators() method registers operator behaviors on a FeatureCell that execute during the Operator stage of the pipeline. Operators evaluate the resolved and merged candidate value before filters, reducers, and taps execute.

Method Contract Summary

  • Operator behaviors are registered declaratively on a FeatureCell instance
  • Operators execute after resolve and merge
  • Operators execute before filters and reducers
  • Operators may forward, modify, or suppress the candidate value
  • Errors propagate as Vault errors

The operators() method defines conditional evaluation and transformation only. It does not mutate existing state, does not emit snapshots, and does not influence pipeline scheduling or lifecycle control. Its responsibility is limited to determining whether, and in what form, the resolved candidate value proceeds to downstream stages.

Note

The operators() method is additive. It may be invoked multiple times, and each invocation appends operator behaviors to the FeatureCell’s operator list. Operators execute in the exact order they are registered during initialization.

While multiple invocations are supported, registering related operators as a single ordered array improves clarity and preserves intentional execution ordering.

Registers operator behaviors that execute during the Operator stage. Operators evaluate resolved and merged candidate values and may forward, modify, or suppress them before downstream stages execute.
Example

The operators() method registers one or more operator behaviors that evaluate resolved and merged candidate values during pipeline execution. Each operator may forward the value unchanged, return a modified value, or suppress further pipeline processing.

What this does

  • Registers one or more operator behaviors on the FeatureCell
  • Operators execute after resolve and merge
  • Operators execute before filters and reducers
  • Suppression short-circuits downstream stages

This demonstrates the intended use of operators() as a declarative mechanism for conditional evaluation, normalization, or suppression prior to filtering and reduction.

Example: Registering Operator Behaviors

{{`
@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {

  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault
      .operators(
        [
          withDistinctUntilChanged()
        ]
      ).initialize();
  }
}
`}}
 
{{`
export const employeeCell = FeatureCell({
  key: 'employees',
  initialState: []
});

employeeCell
  .operators(
    [
      withDistinctUntilChanged()
    ]
  )
  .initialize();
`}}
